Learning Outcomes
1. Identify bones of the axial skeleton and outline their function.
2. Identify and describe the curvatures of the vertebral column
and indicate the function of each.
3. Describe the basic structure of a typical vertebra.
4. Identify the bones of the thoracic wall and describe typical
and atypical ribs.
5. Describe the development of the vertebral column and
muscles of the back.
6. Apply the knowledge of development of the vertebral column
to describe common developmental abnormalities, such as
abnormal curvatures of the vertebral column, spina bifida,
tumours of embryonic origin.

Bones of the axial skeleton
• The axial skeleton consists of 80 bones, that
form the longitudinal axis of the body:
- the skull with 8 cranial bones and 14
facial bones
- bones associated with the skull (ossicles
of the ear and the hyoid bone)
- the vertebral column (24 vertebrae, the
sacrum and the coccyx)
- thoracic cage (24 ribs and the sternum)

Vertebral column (spine)
• The vertebral column in an adult consists of 33
vertebrae, arranged in 5 regions:
- cervical,
- thoracic,
- lumbar,
- sacral and
- coccygeal.
• Movements occur only between 24 vertebrae of
the cervical, thoracic and lumbar region.

Functions of the vertebral column
• Movements
• Supports of the body weight
• Transmits forces through the pelvis to the lower
limbs
• Provides a partly rigid and flexible axis for the
body and a pivot for the head.
• Brace and help manoeuvre upper limbs
• Protects spinal cord and spinal nerves.

Primary and secondary curvatures of the spine
• When viewed from the side, the vertebral column of
a newborn has a C shaped curvature while an adult
has four vertebral curvatures.
• All 4 curvatures are fully developed by the age of
10.
• The primary curvature is concave anteriorly and
remains the same through life in the:
- thoracic and
- sacral region.
• The secondary curvatures appear during infancy
and become concave posteriorly.
- cervical curvature
- lumbar curvature
• Secondary curvatures are also known as a
compensation curvatures as they help shift the
weight to permit an upright position.

Scoliosis
Scoliosis is an abnormal lateral curvature of the
spine.
Common in adolescent girls.
Causes:
- Idiopathic or
- structural malformation of the vertebral
bodies,
- muscle paralysis (such in polio)
-unequal length of lower limbs
- habit scoliosis (habitual standing or
sitting)

Vertebrae
• Vertebrae vary in size and other characteristics
from one region to another.
• Vertebrae of each region can be classified as
typical or atypical.
• A typical vertebra consists of:
- a vertebral body
- a vertebral arch
- seven processes

Typical vertebra
• The body of the vertebra provides strength to the vertebral column and supports body weight.
• Made of vascular trabecular (spongy, cancellous) bone enclosed by a thin external layer of compact
bone; rich in hematopoetic red bone marrow; one or more large foramina posteriorly for basivertebral
veins.
• Superior and inferior surfaces covered with a disc of hyaline cartilage; periphery – epiphyseal rim.

Skeleton of the thoracic wall
• The skeleton of the thoracic wall includes:
- 12 thoracic vertebrae
- 12 pairs of ribs and their costal cartilages
- sternum
• The thoracic skeleton, protects the thoracic
viscera and some abdominal organs and provides
attachments of muscles of respiration, abdominal
wall and back muscles, and movement of the
thorax in respiration and movements of trunk and
back.
• There are three types of ribs:
- true ribs 1-7
- false ribs 8-10
- floating ribs 11 and 12

Typical ribs (3rd to 9th)
• Characteristics of a typical rib:
- head is wedge shaped, with two articular
facets
- neck
- tubercle with the articular facet
- shaft is curved with the costal angle and at
its concave surface it has a costal groove,
that protects intercostal nerve and vessels

Atypical ribs (1st, 2nd , 10th to 12th )
• The first rib is the broadest, nearly horizontal. It
has facet for articulation with T1 vertebral body.
• The grooves are for the subclavian vein anterior
to the scalene tubercle (attachment for the
scalenus anterior muscle) and posterior to the
tubercle a groove for the subclavian artery.
• The 10th to 12th rib have only one facet on their
head for articulation with the vertebral body.
• Costal cartilages prolong ribs anteriorly and
contribute to elasticity of the thoracic wall.

Development of Vertebral Column
• 4th week
• The centrum (primordia of the vertebral body)
forms as the sclerotomal cells migrate ventrally
around the notochord
• The sclerotomal cells around the neural tube
form the vertebral arches
• The sclerotomal cells migrating ventrolaterally
develop into the costal processes

Ossification of Vertebrae
• Ossification begins during the embryonic period (appearance of the primary
ossification centers)
• At birth, each vertebra consists of three bony parts, connected by cartilage
(accommodate growth of the spinal cord).
• The secondary ossification centers appear after puberty and unite around 25 years of
age.

Development of trunk muscles
• Skeletal muscles of the trunk develop from the • http://embryology.med.unsw.edu.au/notes/skmus2.htm
myotome region of the somite
• Each myotome of a somite divides into
- dorsal (epaxial) division
- ventral (hypaxial) division
• Adult derivatives of the epaxial division of the
myotome are intrinsic muscles of the back,
these muscles are supplied by the dorsal rami
of spinal nerves.

Derivatives of epaxial division

vertebral column – Intrinsic muscles of the back:
- Superficial layer (Splenius muscles)
- Intermediate muscles (Erector spinae)
- Deep layer (Transversospinalis muscles)
- in the sacral and coccygeal region myotomes degenerate and
form sacrococcygeal ligament
- What is the nerve supply for these muscles?
posterior rami of the spinal nerves

Spina Bifida
Neurological symptoms are common with severe meningomyelocele:
- paralysys of limbs
- loss of bladder control
- loss of bowel control
- recurrent CNS infections
Prenatal screening:
-pregnancy ultrasound
-amniocentesis
-blood tests (increased levels of alpha fetoprotein)
Prevention:
- folic acid supplements
